rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to retain weakly retained compounds while providing enough final solvent strength to elute strongly retained compounds. The moderate gradient duration and temperature provide a baseline for identifying crowded regions and optimizing subsequent injections.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty while testing how much of the current resolution margin can be traded for speed. Keep temperature and solvent endpoints unchanged to isolate the effect of gradient steepness.

Use an intermediate gradient duration to recover separation in the crowded middle region while targeting a last-peak time below the apparent 10-minute time-penalty threshold. This tests whether gradient duration alone can approach full resolution without a time penalty.

Increase temperature by 5 °C to probe selectivity in the remaining critical pair while retaining the promising 14-minute gradient. This may improve its resolution to at least 1.5 while keeping the last peak below the time-penalty threshold.

The temperature trend suggests the critical pair is approaching an elution-order reversal; testing 55 °C may separate it again on the opposite side. The other gaps appear to offer enough margin, and the last peak should remain below the time-penalty threshold.

Increase gradient steepness modestly at 55 °C to widen the nearly resolved, order-reversed critical pair while preserving the nearby pair’s resolution margin. The strong final solvent and shorter gradient should keep all ten peaks within the penalty-free time window.

Shift both solvent endpoints upward while preserving the successful gradient slope and temperature to test whether initial solvent strength improves the critical-pair margin. Injection 6 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Lengthen injection 7’s gradient to recover resolution in its early critical pair while aiming to preserve the later pair’s separation. This may provide another maximum-score method with more resolution margin than injection 6 and no time penalty.

Test a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient to seek additional critical-pair resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. Injection 8 already attains the maximum CRF, so this tests an alternative optimum rather than a higher score.

Extend injection 9’s gradient by two minutes to lift its limiting resolution above 1.5 while retaining the later pair’s margin. The last peak is expected near 9.5 minutes, potentially yielding another maximum-score method without a time penalty.

Test a higher-temperature alternative with a shallower gradient to balance improved separation of the later critical pair against compression of the earlier pair. The last peak is estimated near 9.8 minutes, potentially preserving the maximum CRF with additional resolution margin.

Reduce the final organic fraction relative to injection 8 to test a slightly shallower gradient at the successful 55 °C temperature. This should improve the earlier critical pair while testing whether the later pair retains baseline resolution, with the last peak still expected below 10 minutes.

Slightly flatten injection 10’s gradient to improve its earlier critical pair while checking that the later pair remains above 1.5. The last peak is projected near 9.8 minutes, potentially retaining the maximum CRF with balanced resolution margins.

Test a gradient slope between injections 7 and 8 to target full resolution with a shorter last-peak time than injection 8. The estimated limiting resolutions are approximately 1.6–1.7, potentially preserving the maximum CRF.

Use a slightly steeper gradient than injection 14 to shorten elution while targeting both critical-pair resolutions above 1.5. The last peak is expected near 7.8 minutes, before the gradient ends, potentially retaining the maximum CRF.

Probe a lower-temperature selectivity regime using the fast gradient from injection 2 to test whether another elution-order change yields full resolution without a time penalty. The maximum CRF is already secured, so this explores an alternative operating region.

Return to the successful 55 °C regime and slightly steepen injection 6’s gradient to target faster elution while preserving full resolution. The last peak is expected before the gradient ends, so the lower final organic fraction should still elute all ten compounds promptly.

Preserve injection 14’s successful gradient slope but end the ramp at 60% organic to test a lower-solvent-strength alternative. Since its last peak eluted at 8.00 minutes, before this shortened gradient reaches the outlet at 8.65 minutes, the maximum CRF should be retained.

Approximate injection 10’s balanced separation using a shorter ramp and lower final organic fraction. Its similar gradient slope should retain both critical-pair resolutions above 1.5 and keep the last peak below 10 minutes, potentially providing another maximum-score method.

Extend injection 8’s gradient to map the slower edge of the maximum-score region. The earlier critical pair should improve, while the later pair is projected to remain near 1.5 and the last peak below 10 minutes.

Slightly steepen injection 19’s gradient to reduce elution time while targeting both critical-pair resolutions above 1.5. This tests a faster alternative within the established maximum-score region, with the last peak projected near 9 minutes.

Preserve injection 17’s gradient slope but transition to a 50% organic hold after the closely spaced peaks have eluted. This tests whether a lower final solvent strength can retain full resolution and keep the last peak below the time-penalty threshold.

Test a slightly steeper gradient than injection 15 followed by a 50% organic hold. This probes the fast-gradient boundary of full resolution while checking whether the final hold still keeps the last peak below 10 minutes.

Use a gradient slope between injections 10 and 13 to target balanced critical-pair resolutions near 1.7 while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. This seeks another maximum-score method with more separation margin than the faster alternatives.

Test a gradient slope between injections 19 and 21, where both critical pairs were fully resolved without a time penalty. This final method is expected to retain the maximum CRF of 1.000, with minimum resolution around 1.6 and the last peak near 9.1 minutes.
